problem_type: Browser File input discarded by a native-path-only asset library drop boundary
symptom: Dragging an image, video, or audio file onto the Web asset library imports nothing and reports no images.
direct_cause: The drop handler converts each File to an absolute native path; browser File has none, so it passes an empty path list to copyFiles.
class_root: The shared drop boundary assumed every host represents a local File with a native filesystem path instead of dispatching by the host's supported import contract.
affected_population: Every ordinary browser File dropped on the Web asset library
Any browser media type accepted by the existing upload endpoint
entry_points: AssetLibraryPanel onDrop dispatches files to useAssetLibraryLocalImport
The same library's paste flow supplies Electron native paths
internal_only_reason: The fix binds this repository's already implemented host bridges; no third-party package behavior determines the invariant.
invariants: Web drops send File bytes through assets.importNativeFile with their original project ID
Electron drops and clipboard paths continue through assets.copyFiles
A failed or malformed per-file import cannot be counted as created

door_reduction.why_not: Both generated doors are read/write uses in the same asset-library import function; copyFiles must remain for Electron native-path imports.

generality_proof: All library File drops converge on the hook's single drop dispatcher. The dispatcher chooses byte upload for Web before native-path extraction, regardless of file name, MIME type, count, or native path absence. Paste remains the separate native-path entrance.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Choose the supported host import operation for every dropped File and aggregate per-file results.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: The panel installs the hook's onDrop handler on the asset library root.
Clipboard paste reads native file paths and has no browser File bytes; it retains the Electron path contract.
Picker drops already preserve the File object for the existing upload API.

recurrence.reason: Every browser File and every future drag repeats the pathless input mechanism.

prevention.invariant: Every browser drop is passed as File bytes to the existing Web bridge while every Electron drop keeps native path copying.
prevention.failure_mode: Unavailable bridge, rejected import, or malformed result increments failed count and never creates an asset.
prevention.strategy: Dispatch all dropped files at one host-aware import boundary and reuse the existing bridge methods.

legacy_paths.rationale: The drop handler's unconditional path-only dispatch is removed; native-path copy remains valid for Electron.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No third-party runtime is changed; existing Web and Electron bridge contracts own import semantics.

migration: No persisted data shape changes. Existing assets remain intact; new Web drops use the existing upload endpoint.
residual_risks: Live zh/en Web and Electron drag verification belongs to coordinator acceptance.

invariant_owner_layer.why: The asset-library drop boundary dispatches every dropped File and owns the Web versus Electron import invariant.
